newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama students clash with police, four injured.
newsitem.headline: Panama students clash with police, four injured.

text.p: Stone-throwing students at the University of Panama clashed with riot police Thursday during a protest against the government's privatization plans.
The demonstration involved some 100 students at the country's largest university and left at least four students slightly injured, witnesses said. There were no immediate reports of arrests.
The students were hit by buckshot and rubber bullets that police fired at the demonstrators.

"We want a radical change from what the government is doing," said a 21-year-old sociology student, who covered his face with a cloth to disguise his identity. "All these plans to privatize government institutions hurt workers and students later on when we go to look for jobs," he said.

The two-year-old administration of President Ernesto Perez Balladares has embarked on a plan to privatize state enterprises and attract foreign investment to ease sluggish growth and a 14-percent unemployment rate.
For the second day running, the protesters blocked traffic along Simon Bolivar Avenue, one of Panama City's main thoroughfares that runs in front of the university.
